In the difficulty-curve editor (`GymCurveSequencer`), add buttons to launch generated level configurations as Gym scenes.

## Requirements

### Reorganise layout
Group waves by level in the curve editor preview. Each level group gets a **Launch Level** button that boots a new dedicated **Level Gym** scene playing all waves in sequence (like campaign mode but in gym context).

### Per-wave launch
Keep a **Launch Wave** button on each individual wave row that plays only that single wave.

### Starting weapons
When launching a level/wave from the curve editor, the player ship starts with:
- **Spread shot** (3-bullet fan at −30°/0°/+30°)
- **Dual shot** (two side-by-side bullets, `±DUAL_SIDE_OFFSET` px perpendicular offset) — the weapon catalogue calls this `dual`.

These should be equipped at scene start (the 'twin shot' mentioned in the original brief = dual).

### Scene details
The Level Gym scene is a new gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (e.g. `GymLevel.ts`). It:
- Takes a level definition (`LevelDefinition`) as its parameter
- Plays all waves sequentially, one after another
- Shows the level name in the HUD
- Provides the spread + dual weapons on start
- Includes a back-to-index button and ESC-to-menu navigation (standard gym pattern)
- Supports launching a single wave (for the per-wave button)

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — new: dedicated level gym scene
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — modify: reorganise waves by level, add launch buttons
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — may need weapon initialisation support for gym context
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — register the new scene
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — read-only: `LevelDefinition` type is already available
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — read-only: weapon catalogue (`spread`, `dual`)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The curve editor preview groups waves by level and renders one **Launch Level** button per level group; activating it boots the Level Gym scene with that level's full `LevelDefinition`.
2. Each wave row renders a **Launch Wave** button that boots the Level Gym scene playing only that single wave.
3. The Level Gym scene plays the launched waves sequentially (level mode) or plays the single launched wave (wave mode).
4. On scene start the player ship is equipped with the **spread** and **dual** weapons (both active and firing).
5. The Level Gym shows the level name in the HUD and provides a back-to-index button plus ESC-to-menu navigation, matching the other gym scenes.
6. Automated tests cover: grouping waves by level, wiring of both launch buttons, sequential wave progression, and the spread + dual starting weapons.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Related work
- AH-0MUITS0VD000DVSV — Campaign builder: config to generated level definitions
- AH-0MUJSUT8P008UPQM — Curve generator: per-wave generation-mode control
- AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4 — GymEnemies: reusable enemy gym scene
- AH-0MUAYB2XR007N10W — GymPlayer: re-based onto shared combat core
- WL-0MULUW9AQ0039RCY — Original misfiled work item (ContextHub prefix `WL`, now deleted)

- **Q1: What does 'each row of the generated level' mean?** — Answer (producer): **B and C** — group waves by level with one Launch Level button per level group, AND keep a Launch Wave button on each wave row for single-wave play. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2: Which weapon is 'twin shot'?** — Answer (producer): **A** — `dual` (two side-by-side bullets). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Which scene should launch?** — Answer (producer): **B** — a new dedicated Level Gym scene that plays the full level definition (all waves in sequence). Source: interactive reply.

# Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice)

## Problem statement

When a run ends, `PlayScene` cuts straight to `GameOverScene`, which renders
identical content for both outcomes — the only difference is a two-word title
(`VICTORY` in green vs `DEFEAT` in red). Victory has no fanfare and no
celebration, and the loss screen gives no distinctive visual or audible signal
that the run is over. The two most consequential moments in the game therefore
feel flat and interchangeable.

## Users

- As a player who has beaten the Central AI boss, I want a triumphant finale
  (fanfare + visual celebration) so that winning feels rewarded.
- As a player who has lost the run, I want a clear, sombre visual and audible
  signal so that defeat feels consequential and is instantly distinguishable
  from victory.
- As a player entering my initials on the game-over screen, I want the
  celebration/defeat treatment to run behind the UI without blocking or
  delaying my keyboard or pointer input.

Example user stories:

- *"I finally beat the boss and the game just… ended. I want it to feel like a
  win — music, sparks, confetti, the lot."*
- *"When I lose I barely notice; the screen looks the same as a win. I want a
  clear 'you lost' moment."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Victory fanfare (audio).** On a run ending in victory (`won: true`) a
   dedicated procedural cue `playVictoryFanfareSound()` plays: a rising major
   arpeggio (≥ 3 distinct notes) resolving into a sustained chord, total
   ~1.5–2.5 s, with a light sparkle/crackle tail. It routes through the master
   SFX gain (so mute/volume apply), peaks at volume ≤ 0.2, and is a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext`. A unit test asserts the scheduled node topology
   and no-throw behaviour headless.
2. **Victory celebration (visual).** A shared module `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`
   exposes `spawnVictoryJuice(...)`, composing at least three layers — a
   celebration particle/confetti burst, one or more expanding shockwave
   ring(s), and a bright flash/glow — all tunable via exported constants with
   per-layer `ENABLE_*` toggles (mirroring `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`). The
   celebration is rendered on `GameOverScene` (victory branch) as a sustained
   treatment behind the score/initials/leaderboard UI. A test asserts the
   layers are created and cleaned up.
3. **Defeat signal (audio + visual).** On defeat (`won: false`)
   `playDefeatStingSound()` plays a descending, sombre cue that is distinct
   from both the victory fanfare and the existing `playPlayerDestructionSound()`,
   and `GameOverScene` renders a distinct defeat treatment (e.g. red vignette
   plus a desaturation/glitch flicker) that appears only on the defeat branch.
   A test asserts defeat-only objects/cues are present for `won: false` and
   absent for `won: true`.
4. **Non-blocking, lifecycle-safe, graceful.** The treatments never intercept,
   delay or block keyboard/pointer input on `GameOverScene` — initials entry
   and Return to Menu remain fully usable throughout. Every juice display
   object is tracked in a scene-owned registry destroyed on `SHUTDOWN` (no
   leaks across scene restart). The defeat treatment layers on top of the
   existing in-run *fatal* death juice (`spawnPlayerDeathJuice`) without
   replacing or weakening it. All new cues are safe no-ops without an
   `AudioContext`.
5. **Parity and documentation.** Any behaviour shared with scene paths that can
   reach a run end is implemented once and consumed by both (per the
   AGENTS.md gym↔game parity convention); where a gym has no run-end screen,
   the reason is documented. `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 (visual
   style / juice) and §7.3 (SFX catalogue + Player Audio Character) are updated
   with the new victory/defeat treatment and cue entries, and new tunables are
   documented in code comments.
6. **Tests and full suite.** Unit tests cover victory/defeat audio synthesis
   (node topology, volume ceiling, safe no-op headless), juice composition and
   teardown, outcome-branch rendering, and non-blocking input. `GameOverScene.test.ts`
   is extended. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Procedural Web Audio only, zero external audio assets** (GDD §7.3); the
  new cues follow the existing `src/audio/effects.ts` synthesis style.
- **No background music** — background music is explicitly out of MVP scope
  (GDD §7.3). The victory treatment is SFX + VFX only.
- **Player cue volume ceiling ≤ 0.2**, routed through the master SFX gain so
  the Settings mute and volume controls apply.
- **Safe no-op without an `AudioContext`** (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
  browsers) — audio must never be a hard dependency.
- **Non-blocking**: the treatment is cosmetic only and must not delay or
  interfere with leaderboard/initials input. Gameplay, scoring and leaderboard
  behaviour are unchanged.
- **Canvas/palette**: 960×540 near-black palette (GDD §7.1) — cyan/green for
  victory, red/desaturated for defeat.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- **Browser autoplay policy** (GDD §6.7): `GameOverScene` is only reached after
  the player has interacted (Start/Play), so the `AudioContext` is already
  unlocked; no new unlock path is required.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._finishRun(won)` calls `scene.start('GameOverScene', { won, score })`.
  Victory is triggered from `_damageBoss()` (boss destroyed) → `_finishRun(true)`;
  defeat from `_loseLife()` when lives reach zero → `_finishRun(false)`.
- On the fatal defeat path, `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(this, x, y, 'fatal', …)` and
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()` already fire *before* the transition
  (`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), but the scene switch stops `PlayScene`
  almost immediately, so the GameOver screen carries no lasting treatment.
- `GameOverScene` (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`) renders a black rectangle, a
  coloured `VICTORY`/`DEFEAT` title, the final score, optional initials entry,
  the leaderboard, and Return to Menu — otherwise identical for both outcomes.
- No victory-specific audio or VFX exists anywhere; `src/audio/effects.ts` has
  no victory/defeat cue.
- Juice precedent: `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` and `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`
  use a pure `resolve*Params()` + exported tunables + per-layer `ENABLE_*`
  toggles + a caller-owned effects registry cleared on `SHUTDOWN`.
- Audio precedent: every cue in `src/audio/effects.ts` routes through
  `ensureMasterGain(ctx)` and degrades to a no-op without an `AudioContext`.

## Desired change

- Add two procedural cues to `src/audio/effects.ts`:
  - `playVictoryFanfareSound()` — rising major arpeggio + sustained chord +
    sparkle tail.
  - `playDefeatStingSound()` — descending sombre sting (+ optional filtered
    noise tail), distinct from the hull-breach cue.
  Both exported with `VICTORY_*` / `DEFEAT_*` tunable constants, volume ≤ 0.2.
- Add a shared end-of-run juice module `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` with a pure
  `resolveEndOfRunJuiceParams(outcome)` mapping and `spawnVictoryJuice(...)`
  (plus the defeat screen treatment) built from layered, individually
  switchable effects.
- Trigger the victory fanfare at the moment of the win in `PlayScene`, and
  render the sustained celebration on `GameOverScene`'s victory branch so it
  remains visible for the whole screen without introducing a long blocking
  delay before the transition.
- Render the defeat treatment and play the defeat sting on `GameOverScene`'s
  defeat branch, layered on top of the existing in-run fatal death juice.
- Keep the treatment behind the existing UI; wire all juice objects into a
  registry cleaned up on `SHUTDOWN`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` — **New**: shared victory/defeat juice composition,
  pure params resolver, tunables, per-layer toggles and effect registry.
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.test.ts` — **New**: unit tests for params, layer
  composition and teardown.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — **Edit**: add `playVictoryFanfareSound()` /
  `playDefeatStingSound()` and their exported constants.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — **Edit**: tests for the new cues (topology,
  volume ceiling, no-throw headless).
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — **Edit**: render victory/defeat treatment
  behind the UI; trigger the defeat sting; own and clear the effect registry.
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` — **Edit**: outcome-branch rendering,
  teardown and non-blocking-input tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit**: trigger the victory fanfare/celebration
  at the moment of the win.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: §7.2 (juice) and §7.3 (SFX
  catalogue / Player Audio Character); §4.5/§5.1 only if flow notes change.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Motion/flash discomfort* — flashes, glitch flicker and particles can be
  uncomfortable. Mitigation: keep layers short, reuse the existing tunable
  patterns, keep per-layer `ENABLE_*` toggles; a reduce-motion accessibility
  option is a separate (linked) work item, not part of this scope.
- *Scene-transition timing* — existing tests assume `GameOverScene` is active
  ~350 ms after boss defeat (`PlayScene.test.ts`), so a long in-run hold would
  break them. Mitigation: compose the *sustained* celebration on
  `GameOverScene` (no long blocking delay); keep any in-run flourish short and
  update timing-sensitive tests deliberately.
- *Audio overlap / clipping* — the fanfare must not drown other cues or clip.
  Mitigation: ≤ 0.2 peak, single one-shot through the master gain.
- *Parity convention* — `GameOverScene` is currently only reached from
  `PlayScene`; gyms have no run-end screen. Mitigation: keep the shared helper
  in `src/vfx/`, document the justified absence of a gym consumer, and run the
  parity/docs assertions.
- *Scope creep* — "loads of juice" could expand into background music, a
  cutscene or a leaderboard redesign. Mitigation: keep to SFX + VFX + screen
  treatment; capture extras as linked work items, not scope.
- *Pre-existing flaky test* — AH-0MUINWNPI000G6MU (boss victory → return to
  menu) fails under full-suite parallel load; not caused by this work, but the
  suite must be green before finishing.

**Assumptions** (producer-validatable)

- *Victory* means `won: true` (the boss was defeated); *defeat* means
  `won: false`. There is no other run-end path.
- No background music is added (GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope).
- The treatment is purely cosmetic: score, lives, leaderboard and initials
  entry are unchanged.
- The primary consumer is `PlayScene` → `GameOverScene`; gyms do not reach a
  run-end screen, so no gym behaviour change is required (documented).

## Related work

See the automated "Related work (automated report)" section below (added by the
`find-related` skill).

- Need juice when the player is destroyed (AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY) — *completed*;
  provides the in-run fatal death juice this work layers on top of and must
  stay visually distinct from.
- Phase shift needs to be auto-applied when needed (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8) —
  *completed*; precedent for a dedicated cue + screen overlay that was
  deliberately kept distinct from death juice.
- Integrate boss encounter into PlayScene (AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ) — *completed*;
  owns the `won: true` victory trigger.
- Implement GameOverScene — scoring, lives, game-over flow (AH-0MU731426003FE71)
  — *completed*; the screen to be dressed.
- Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J)
  — *open*; if it lands first, the new cues should follow its pattern. Risk,
  not a blocker.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fanfare/juice live?** Options: (A) both an in-run
  flourish and a persistent `GameOverScene` treatment; (B) in-run only;
  (C) `GameOverScene` only.
  — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **A** — both layers. Rationale
  recorded: an immediate moment-of-win/loss payoff plus a screen that keeps
  celebrating while the player enters initials. The agent's recommended option
  was A.
- **Q2 — Victory audio character and scope?** Options: (A) procedural
  multi-note fanfare + sparkle tail; (B) a single short sting; (C) fanfare
  plus a looping victory music track.
  — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **A** — procedural multi-note
  fanfare. Rationale: delivers "loads of fanfare" within MVP constraints
  (Web Audio only, no music).
- **Q3 — How strong/distinct should the defeat treatment be?** Options:
  (A) distinct sombre screen treatment (red vignette + desaturation/glitch
  flicker + descending sting) layered on the existing in-run death juice;
  (B) rely on the existing death juice only; (C) add strong camera shake /
  heavy flashes to defeat too.
  — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **A** — distinct sombre screen
  treatment. Rationale: the ask explicitly wants an audible *and* visual loss
  signal while keeping it clearly distinct from the victory celebration.

### Assumption confirmations (recorded, not blocking)

- The treatment never blocks or delays initials entry / Return to Menu.
- The treatment respects the existing SFX mute and volume.
- All cues degrade to a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- Shared behaviour is consumed by both the game and the gyms where applicable;
  `GameOverScene` is not reached from a gym, so no gym run-end behaviour
  changes (documented).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUAYB957002EMYV** – Divers should not return (completed)
- **AH-0MTGS8EK8007TTQC** – Add player pickup activation audio to effects.ts (completed)
- **AH-0MTGS4P0V005MTSN** – Add 4 player shoot audio cues to effects.ts (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, absent, active, add, added (+371 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, absent, acceptance, active, add (+363 more)

# Reduce the starting range of all weapons by 50%

## Problem statement

Player weapon ranges are currently tuned so that bullets reach roughly a
third to two-thirds of the playfield before expiring, and AOE weapons resolve
within a 70–120 px radius. The operator wants the **starting (base) range of
every player weapon halved** so engagements are closer and the screen is less
saturated by long-lived wrapped bullets. The reduction must also flow through
to weapon-leveling upgrades, so the effective range at *every* weapon level is
50% of today's value.

## Users

- **Players** — get closer-range combat where shots feel more deliberate and
  the playfield is less cluttered by wraparound bullets; AOE coverage is
  tighter and more positional.
- **Designers / AI agents** — need a single, unambiguous source of truth for
  each weapon's range so balance tuning does not diverge between the game and
  the gyms.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my weapons to have a shorter reach so that I must
  commit to closing distance with enemies instead of picking them off across
  the whole screen.
- As a **player**, I want AOE weapons (Nova, Mortar, Arc) to cover a smaller
  area so positioning matters more.
- As a **developer**, I want the range reduction defined in one place (the
  base lifespan / AOE radii constants) so it stays consistent across the game
  and every gym, and so weapon leveling keeps working unchanged on top.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Base player-weapon ranges halved.** Every value in
  `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) is halved, so effective
  range (`BULLET_SPEED` 350 px/s × lifetime) is halved: Cannon 1.5→**0.75 s**
  (~262.5 px), Spread 1.4→**0.7 s** (~245 px), Dual 1.4→**0.7 s** (~245 px),
  Rapid 0.75→**0.375 s** (~131 px), Nova 0.5→**0.25 s**, Mortar 2.0→**1.0 s**,
  Arc 0.5→**0.25 s**. Verified by unit tests asserting the exported catalogue
  values.
- [ ] **AC2 — AOE radii halved.** Every value in `AOE_RADII`
  (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) is halved: Nova 90→**45 px**, Mortar 70→**35 px**,
  Arc 120→**60 px**, and each catalogue `aoe.radius` reflects the new value.
  Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Leveled ranges are also halved.** Because
  `resolveWeaponDefinition` (`src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`) applies *relative*
  level multipliers (`bulletLifetime` up to 2.2×, `aoeRadius`) to the base
  catalogue values, halving the base halves the absolute range at **every**
  level. The leveling curve specs (bases, caps, `k`, tiers) are **not**
  changed. Verified by tests asserting `resolveWeaponDefinition(id, level)`
  yields half the pre-change `bulletLifetime` / `aoe.radius` at level 0 and at
  the capped level.
- [ ] **AC4 — Player-bullet fallback default halved.** The default `lifetime`
  in `PlayerBullet`'s constructor and `createPlayerBullet`
  (`src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`) is reduced 1.5→**0.75 s** so the fallback
  matches the reduced Cannon default. Verified by unit test.
- [ ] **AC5 — Enemy bullets unchanged.** Enemy bullet lifetimes (e.g.
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `BaseEnemy`, entity configs) are **not**
  modified; this item covers player weapons only. Verified by tests asserting
  enemy lifetimes retain their current values.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4
  (bullet-range note and weapon/AOE table radii: Nova 90→45 px, Arc 120→60 px,
  Mortar 70→35 px) and any affected code comments reflect the new values.
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation.** New/updated unit tests cover: halved base
  lifetimes (AC1), halved AOE radii (AC2), halved leveled ranges (AC3), the
  reduced fallback default (AC4), and unchanged enemy lifetimes (AC5). The
  existing player-weapon, AOE, and weapon-leveling suites continue to pass.
- [ ] **AC8 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Test suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
  changes.

## Constraints

- **Player weapons only** (operator decision Q1): enemy bullet lifetimes are
  out of scope and must not change.
- **AOE included** (operator decision Q2): Nova/Mortar/Arc radii are halved.
- **Leveling included** (operator decision Q3): the 50% reduction applies at
  every weapon level; implemented by halving the base values so the relative
  level multipliers carry through. The leveling curve specs themselves are
  unchanged.
- Range stays expressed as a **lifetime in seconds** / **AOE radius in px**;
  no new coupling to `bulletSpeed` or pixel budgets.
- Fire rates, shot patterns, bullet speeds, colours, and drop behaviour are
  unchanged.
- Applies to both the game (`PlayScene` / `src/scenes/core/`) and all gyms via
  the single shared catalogue (gym↔game parity convention).

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME` (per-weapon seconds) and
  `AOE_RADII` (px) are the single source of truth; `BULLET_SPEED = 350`;
  effective range = `BULLET_SPEED × bulletLifetime`.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `resolveWeaponDefinition` multiplies base
  `bulletLifetime` by the `bulletLifetime` level multiplier and base
  `aoe.radius` by the `aoeRadius` level multiplier; multipliers are relative
  (base 1, so level 0 = base).
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — default `lifetime` = 1.5 s in the
  constructor and `createPlayerBullet`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — spawns player bullets using
  `def.bulletLifetime` from the (possibly level-resolved) weapon definition.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 documents the per-weapon lifetimes and
  the Nova/Arc AOE radii.

## Desired change

1. Halve every entry in `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME` and `AOE_RADII` in
   `src/utils/weapons.ts`.
2. Halve the `PlayerBullet` / `createPlayerBullet` default `lifetime`.
3. Leave `weaponLevels.ts` multipliers and every enemy-config lifetime
   unchanged.
4. Update the GDD §4.4 range/radius figures and affected code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — halve `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME` and `AOE_RADII`
  values; update their doc comments (Cannon ~262 px, etc.).
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — default `lifetime` 1.5→0.75 in the
  constructor and factory, plus doc comments.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — assert new base lifetimes and radii.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` — assert leveled ranges are 50% of the
  pre-change absolute values.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.test.ts` — assert the reduced fallback default.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` / `bulletLifecycle.test.ts` — update
  any expectations pinned to the old radii/lifetimes.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 range figures and AOE radius table.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — *Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen* (completed). Established the per-weapon `bulletLifetime`
  range model and already halved the lifetimes once (the current 1.5 s Cannon
  baseline). This item halves them again. Strong precedent for both the
  approach and the files touched.
- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — *Weapon leveling* (in-progress). Owns
  `resolveWeaponDefinition` and the `bulletLifetime` / `aoeRadius` level
  multipliers this item deliberately leaves unchanged (their output halves
  automatically). Coordinate if that item is landing concurrently
  (related-to).
- **AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD** — *Area of effect weapons* (completed). Established
  `AOE_RADII`; this item scales its values.
- **AH-0MUQUTRWT008OERQ** — *F4: Arc weapon — chaining bolts* (completed) —
  Arc's 120 px chain radius is reduced here.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 — range and AOE tuning baseline.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQUTRWT008OERQ** – F4: Arc weapon — chaining bolts (completed)
- **AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51** – Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (blocked)
- **AH-0MTBOE8JM0040Z3Y** – Pure helper: MovementInput → {firingEngines, flameScales} (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: aoe, bullet, bullets, current, down (+11 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: aoe, bullet, bullets, current, down (+11 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: aoe, bullet, bullets, current, down (+9 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope (confirmed):** player weapons only, enemy bullets untouched (Q1).
- **AOE (confirmed):** radii halved alongside lifetimes (Q2).
- **Leveling (confirmed, interpretation documented):** "everything, including
  per-level range increases" (Q3). Implemented by halving the base values;
  because level multipliers are relative, the absolute range at every level is
  halved without editing `weaponLevels.ts`. If the intent was instead to
  reduce the leveling *bonus percentage* (multiplier caps), that is a
  different change — flag during review.
- **AOE range semantics:** Nova and Arc spawn no travelling bullet, so their
  sole "range" is the AOE radius; Mortar has both a travel range (lifetime ×
  180 px/s) and a blast radius — both are halved here.
- **Difficulty risk:** shorter range generally makes the game harder (less
  standoff); values may need playtesting. All values remain individually
  tunable constants with no architectural change.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not retune fire rates, bullet speeds, enemy
  lifetimes, drop rates, or the leveling curve here — record as separate
  linked work items.
- **Test-churn risk:** gym/AOE suites may pin the old radii/lifetimes; update
  expectations in the same change to keep gym↔game parity green.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (round 1): "Does this 50% reduction apply to enemy bullets as well, or
  only to player weapons?" — Answer (operator): **"Only players"**. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q2 (round 1): "The AOE weapons (Nova, Mortar, Arc) have effective range
  defined by their blast radius rather than bullet lifetime. Should those
  radii be reduced by 50% too?" — Answer (operator): **"yes"**. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q3 (round 1): "Does 'starting range' mean (a) only the base values with
  weapon leveling multipliers building on top, or (b) everything including any
  per-level range increases?" — Answer (operator): **"b"** — everything,
  including per-level range increases. Source: interactive reply. Research:
  `resolveWeaponDefinition` (`src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`) applies relative
  multipliers to the base catalogue values, so halving the base halves the
  absolute range at every level with no multiplier-curve edit.
